title: The Sovereignty of God Ministers to the Anxious Heart
speaker: Isaiah Couch
series: Calm in the Character of God

outline.title: The Biblical Definition of Anxiety
subpoints: Anxiety is defined biblically as sin
The command to 'do not worry' in Matthew 6
The call to seek first the Kingdom of God

outline.title: The Personal Testimony of Doubt and Restoration
subpoints: Personal struggle with anxiety after a vehicle accident
The danger of viewing God as limited or indifferent
The comfort of God's unchanging sovereignty

outline.title: The Nature of God's Sovereignty: Omniscience
subpoints: God knows the macro and micro details of creation
Comfort in knowing God cares for individual circumstances
The precision of God's knowledge as a source of peace

outline.title: The Nature of God's Sovereignty: Aseity
subpoints: God is never needy, surprised, or weakened
Freedom from the burden of holding everything together

summary:
This Sunday school lesson continues the series 'Calm in the Character of God,' focusing on how the doctrine of God's sovereignty ministers to the anxious heart. The speaker, Isaiah Couch, begins by defining anxiety biblically as sin, referencing the Lord's command in Matthew 6 to seek first the Kingdom of God rather than worrying about tomorrow. He emphasizes that true peace comes not from worldly coping mechanisms, but from fixing one's eyes on the sovereign, eternal, and unchangeable God.

Couch shares a personal testimony of struggling with anxiety and doubt following a vehicle accident, illustrating the temptation to question God's control. He counters this by pointing to Isaiah 46, where God declares His uniqueness and ability to declare the end from the beginning. This leads to the central thesis: true comfort is found in trusting the One who is sovereign over all creation, aligning with the first question of the Heidelberg Catechism regarding our only comfort in life and death.

The lesson breaks down the nature of God's sovereignty into two key aspects: omniscience and aseity. Through omniscience, as seen in Psalm 139, believers find comfort in knowing that God is aware of and cares for the intimate details of their lives. Through aseity, or self-existence, as seen in Exodus 3, believers are freed from the anxiety of feeling responsible for holding everything together, recognizing that God is self-sufficient, never needy, and never surprised by circumstances.
